 Umno wants govt to explain declassified minutes on pardon decision
 Umno wants govt to explain declassified minutes on pardon decision
 18-Nov-2026, 16:51 18 Nov 2026, 16:51 FMT Reporters Share Among others, Umno information chief Azalina Othman Said asks who decided to declassify the document and when.
 The declassified minutes of the FTPB meeting revealed that Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar, federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh and two other FTPB members were against allowing Najib Razak to be placed under house arrest through a conditional pardon. 
 PETALING JAYA : Umno has urged the government to disclose details on the declassification of the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) meeting minutes on Najib Razak’s conditional pardon. 
 Umno information chief Azalina Othman Said pointed out that home minister Saifuddin Nasution Ismail had said on Nov 12 the proposal to declassify the document would be brought to the Cabinet.
 However, on Nov 13, government spokesman Fahmi Fadzil said the proposal had not been “directly” raised yet, she said.
 “For a classified document, the decision to declassify it must be made by the relevant public officer under Section 2C of the Official Secrets Act according to the set procedures.
 “Following the circulation of the (FTPB meeting minutes) to the public, Umno urges the responsible authority to offer an official explanation on the matter,” she said in a statement.
 Azalina, who is also the law and institutional reform minister, questioned whether the minutes were “officially declassified”, and that if they were, the relevant authority should reveal who made the decision and when.
 She said the public officer should also disclose the basis and purpose of the declassification and the procedures followed.
 “Does the copy being circulated match the official document? Does the declassification cover the entire minutes, including the appendix, or only certain sections?” she said, stressing the importance of transparency in handling the FTPB’s records.
 According to Malaysiakini, the FTPB meeting minutes were declassified following the Bar Council’s legal challenge against Najib’s house arrest under his conditional pardon.
 A well-placed source had also confirmed to FMT that the document was declassified.
 The minutes revealed that Attorney-General Dusuki Mokhtar, federal territories minister Hannah Yeoh and two other FTPB members were against allowing Najib to be placed under house arrest through the pardon.
 The pardon was subject to Najib paying his reduced RM50 million fine for his SRC International conviction.
 The former prime minister was placed under house arrest on Nov 10 after Umno helped pay the RM50 million fine through crowdfunding.
